cluster_name: North Korea fires ballistic missile; Japan confirms fall outside EEZ
event_summary: North Korea launched a possible ballistic missile on August 6, 2026, which Japan's Defense Ministry confirmed fell outside Japan's exclusive economic zone. South Korea's prime minister called for drone, AI, and cyber attack scenarios to be added to the ongoing Ulchi civil defense exercises.
tldr: The most striking finding is that South Korea's two largest newspapers — conservative Chosun Ilbo and progressive Hankyoreh — both entirely ignored the North Korean missile launch in their available signal items, instead running baseball heat-wave cancellations and domestic health and aviation stories. Japan's three outlets (Asahi, Mainichi, NHK) anchored uniformly on Defense Ministry EEZ status language, indicating a coordinated government notification drove press coverage. South Korea's Yonhap wire bridged the two events, publishing the Japan Defense Ministry statement in Korean (idx 9) while its English arm separately covered Ulchi exercise modernization calling for drone, AI, and cyber scenarios (idx 10). This two-country, seven-outlet cluster shows wire services carrying the security story across both countries and languages while flagship Korean papers exercised editorial discretion toward domestic civilian concerns.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to explicitly link the Ulchi civil defense exercise to modern threat scenarios (drone, AI, cyber), connecting South Korea's defensive posture to the day's security context.
Only corpus item to provide procedural detail: Japan's Defense Ministry confirmed on the afternoon of August 6 that the object had not entered Japan's EEZ as of that time.
South Korea's largest conservative daily ran both available signal items on KBO baseball cancellations due to record heat, with no missile-launch coverage in the cluster.
South Korea's leading progressive outlet ran a rare liver disease (PFIC) patient guidebook and a Boeing 777 cargo conversion story — no security coverage despite the missile launch.

coverage_caveats.reason: bucket carried 0 items today (rolling 7-day avg 50.0). Feeds 403'd / timed out / returned empty. Treat absence as structural, not editorial.

bottom_line: Japan's press unified behind Defense Ministry EEZ language on the North Korean missile launch, while South Korean flagship outlets in this cluster covered baseball heat-wave suspensions and domestic stories rather than the launch. Wire services (Yonhap) carried the security story across both countries and languages, and also surfaced the parallel Ulchi exercise modernization call — situating the missile launch within South Korea's broader defensive evolution toward drone, AI, and cyber threat scenarios.
